newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Garovaglio buys 70% stake in food firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Garovaglio buys 70% stake in food firm.

text.p: Argentine holding company Garovaglio & Zorraquin announced Monday it has agreed to buy a 70 percent stake in leading local meat processor and exporter Compania Elaboradora de Productos Alimenticios (CEPA) for $84 million.
The purchase scheduled to take place July 31 is subject to the due diligence, and final approval by Garovaglio's board, Garovaglio told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter.
CEPA has two meat factories in Buenos Aires and one in Santa Fe province. In 1996 it posted revenues for $214 million.

Under the conditions for the deal Garovaglio would also control leather firm Grumbam (1996 revenues $60 million), protein producer Willmor (1996 revenues $20 million) and can maker Argenvases (1996 revenues $3.4 million).
CEPA and these three other firms have a total payroll of 2,500.
